title: Adaptive kernel plugging for sparse attention and prefill traffic
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce 99th-percentile prefill and decode latency and smooth inter-GPU bandwidth by dynamically selecting attention/GEMM kernels and throttling prefill traffic when attention sparsity or memory pressure indicate it will reduce NCCL contention. This ticket implements an adaptive 'kernel plug' controller that can hot-swap kernel paths (dense, block-sparse, grouped-QK, fused attention) per-layer and per-stage and coordinate microbatch pacing across tensor/pipeline parallel ranks.
description_details:
Motivation:
- Many customer workloads have mixed attention patterns (long prefix prefill followed by short decode) causing transient spikes in NCCL allreduce/alltoall traffic during prefill.
- Static kernel selection wastes cycles when sparsity-friendly kernels could reduce compute and comm cost.
- A lightweight controller that observes per-GPU memory pressure, attention sparsity, sequence length distribution, and in-flight NCCL queue depth can choose kernels and emit pacing hints to neighboring ranks to avoid simultaneous burst traffic.
Design approach:
- Observability: lightweight counters and micro-profilers per-GPU (attention sparsity histogram, KV cache footprint delta, NCCL queue depth estimate).
- Decision logic: rule+ML hybrid: start with deterministic heuristics (sparsity > 0.6 && KV delta small => switch to block-sparse kernel; if NCCL inflight > threshold => apply bandwidth-adaptive throttling).
- Kernel plugging: expose an abstract kernel selector in runtime that supports safe mid-request kernel transitions at layer boundaries and encodes fallbacks.
- Coordination: low-overhead broadcast channel (in-band gRPC heartbeat) between pipeline ranks for short-term pacing signals (20-200ms windows).
- Safety/fallbacks: if kernel fails or memory fragmentations rise, revert to baseline dense kernels and trigger regeneration telemetry.
Success metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Reduce prefill 99th latency by >=10% on heterogeneous 4-GPU setups for long-sequence workloads (8k tokens prefill).
- Keep average GPU utilization >= baseline and reduce NCCL tail queue lengths by >=15%.
- No test case should see increased error rates or correctness regressions.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-customer cohort.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks show >=10% 99th reduction on target workloads; integration tests for kernel swap at layer boundaries; end-to-end smoke on Dedicated with rollout flag; updated console dashboard for new metrics.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for kernel selector logic. 2) Staging cluster microbench: 4xA100 hetero bandwidth and two sequence shapes (prefill-heavy, decode-heavy). 3) Canary rollout to 5 customers on Dedicated for 72 hours with QA alerting on regressions. 4) Comparative traces stored in perf-dashboard (dashboard link below).
rollout_plan: Feature gated boolean: false by default. Canary cohort (internal + 5 early customers) -> expand to 25% Dedicated -> 100% Dedicated -> consider enabling for hosted API with opt-in. Rollback policy: immediate disable flag; automatically revert to dense kernels if error signals exceed threshold.
notes: This ticket focuses on runtime control and kernel selection; separate follow-ups will address automatic kernel compilation and new quantized kernels. Coordinate with model-onboarding and Optimize teams for workload cataloging.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Chen: Initial spike: profiled long-prefill LLaMA2-13B runs. Observed 18% NCCL tail queue growth during prefill boundaries. Drafted controller design and heuristics.

2026-03-02 - Diego Alvarez: Prototype kernel selector integrated into staging runtime. Added API to register 'sparsity hints' from attention op. Implemented safe layer-boundary swap with checksum validation.

2026-03-05 - Performance: Staging 4xA100 run (8k prefill) showed 8% reduction in 99th latency and 12% reduction in NCCL queue metric after enabling block-sparse kernel + pacing; baseline fallback paths intact.

2026-03-08 - PR feedback (runtime team): Request to reduce heartbeat frequency and move pacing signals to in-band control plane to avoid extra RPCs. Linting and unit tests requested for selector policy table.
2026-03-12 - QA: Added regression tests for kernel swap under memory pressure. Next: run canary on Dedicated cluster slice and run longer tail experiments (48h).
Next steps: finalize heuristics, add opt-in ML policy trainer (separate ticket), prepare canary runbooks and alert thresholds.
